findings.where: /home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/frozen/oracle_scripts_staging/c28_users/run_campaigns.sh:19-25 (no start guard; first destructive lines are 40-41); compare /home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/frozen/oracle_scripts_staging/c26_ec/c26.sh:14-15
findings.problem: No single-instance or stray-client guard. If it is started while another run_campaigns.sh or an old replay_programs.py is alive (a relaunch after a partial hand stop, or after a false 'launcher not running' alert), it stops the running arm's server, wipes its SSD store and boots a new server on port 30000. The other client keeps going: its requests fail while the port is down, then land on the new arm's server under the same tag, so the same rids and session names. Neither client's records show it, and the first launcher still finds a summary line and writes DONE (next finding). c26.sh refused to start in this situation; the new launcher dropped that protection. Nothing is running now (03:26Z: no server, client or launcher), so this bites on relaunches.
findings.evidence: c26.sh:14-15: `for i in $(seq 1 60); do pgrep -f '^bash run_compare.sh' > /dev/null || break; sleep 10; done` / `if pgrep -f '^bash run_compare.sh' > /dev/null; then echo "C26 STOP ...: run_compare.sh is still running"; exit 1; fi`. run_campaigns.sh goes from line 19 `cd "$AC/scripts" || exit 1` straight to the folder loop; every arm then runs line 40 `bash stop_server.sh` and line 41 `find /mnt/ssd/hicache_l3 -mindepth 1 -delete`. watch.sh:30 reads any failing `docker exec ... pgrep` as "ALERT: launcher not running", which invites a relaunch on top of a live launcher. Scratch test of the guard below (bash 5.2.21): second instance prints "STOP: already running as pid 23354"; a stale pid file, a pid file naming the wrapper parent, and a non-existent pid all pass. The `bash -c 'nohup bash ... >> log 2>&1'` wrapper stays alive as the parent with the script name in its command line, hence the $PPID exclusion.
findings.fix:
Insert after line 19 of run_campaigns.sh:
PIDF=$AC/results/.run_campaigns.pid; old=$(cat "$PIDF" 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$old" ] && [ "$old" != "$$" ] && [ "$old" != "$PPID" ]; then
  case "$(tr '\0' ' ' 2>/dev/null < "/proc/$old/cmdline")" in *run_campaigns.sh*) echo "STOP: run_campaigns.sh is already running as pid $old"; exit 1 ;; esac
fi
echo $$ > "$PIDF"
if pgrep -f 'python[0-9.]* [r]eplay_(programs|agentic)\.py' > /dev/null; then
  echo "STOP: a replay client is still running and would send to this campaign's servers (pkill -f '[r]eplay_programs.py')"; exit 1
fi
And make watch.sh:30 ask twice before alerting:
  docker exec sglang_hicache pgrep -f '[r]un_campaigns.sh' > /dev/null || { sleep 10; docker exec sglang_hicache pgrep -f '[r]un_campaigns.sh' > /dev/null; } || { echo "ALERT: launcher not running"; exit 0; }

findings.problem: An arm is DONE as soon as client.jsonl holds a summary line, whatever the summary says. If the server dies or starts failing mid-arm, the client records one error per request, keeps going to the 7,200 s deadline and writes its summary; the launcher then writes DONE, adds the manifest line (so a resume never reruns the arm) and starts the next arm. The DONE line carries no request or error count, so the watcher's printout cannot show it either. Arms 1 and 2 are the likely place (see the finding on engine coverage).

DONE`. Real summary line (today's probe): `{"kind":"summary","tag":"tl_ours_x10_a01",...,"profile":621,"warmup":0,"errors":0,...}`. findings.problem: The SSD cleaner will probably fire inside the 2-hour window for the first time in these campaigns, at a time that differs by arm. It deletes the oldest-written pages first, whether or not a live session still needs them. Expected fill after 2 h: campaign 29 about 75-86 % of the volume (first pass near minute 98-112); campaign 28 about 57-73 % (only the faster arms cross 70 %, in the last minutes). A session admitted in the first quarter hour and still alive then loses its first pages on SSD and recomputes its whole prompt on return. The effect is small in aggregate but lands on long-lived returning sessions, and some arms would get a pass while others would not.
findings.evidence: Cleaner order: `ordered = sorted((group ...), key=lambda group: group.mtime)`, triggered when `pct >= self.high_watermark`; reads do not refresh mtime. Calibration from the probe that ended 03:06Z (TraceLab, 0.1 users/s, 44 users, x10): df showed 377.0 GB used for 3.92M new tokens (prompt - ideal_cached + output over its 621 requests) = 96 KB per new token, 246 MB/s. Campaign 26 never reached the mark: `grep -c 'NIXL L3 cleanup'` is 0 in its 128-user arms, and iostat_vdc.log sums to 1,400-1,410 GB written (57 %). New tokens from the traces (seed-0 arrival sets): TraceLab 17.3K per first prompt plus 3.4K per later request; FreeInference 10.8K plus 1.36K. At the throughput campaign 27 measured (30-35 requests/min TraceLab; 66-86/min FreeInference by a capacity model) that is 18.7-21.6M tokens (1.84-2.12 TB) and 14.3-18.2M (1.41-1.79 TB). The 70 % mark is 1.72 TB of 2,456 GB.
findings.fix: Line 42: change `L3_CLEANER_PCT=70,60` to `L3_CLEANER_PCT=90,80` (2.21 TB; 245 GB of headroom against at most 12 GB written per 30 s cleaner tick). findings.problem: Conditional on the container's aiohttp version, which I could not read without docker. The server streams /generate cumulatively: every token sends one line carrying all output ids and all text so far. The client reads by line, and aiohttp refuses a line longer than twice read_bufsize. With a 64 KiB default (131,072-byte lines) outputs beyond roughly 10-21K tokens fail mid-generation after 10-25 minutes of decode; the request is recorded as an error and watch.sh exits at the first error, then exits again on every restart for the rest of that arm. No earlier run streamed more than 7,318 output tokens, so this path is untested either way.
findings.evidence: Server args of the 02:38Z boot: `'stream_interval': 1`, `'incremental_streaming_output': False`; tokenizer_manager.py:1892-1898 fills `out["text"] = state.get_text()` on every chunk, with `"output_ids": state.output_ids`. The aiohttp 3.14.4 copy on this host: `self._high_water = limit * 2`, `if chunk_size > max_size: raise LineTooLong`, `read_bufsize: int = DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE` (2**18, so 512 KiB lines, safe); releases I know through 3.13 default to 2**16. Ids alone are at least 6 bytes a token. Outputs in the seed-0 arrival sets: FreeInference 21,209 and 18,360 (arrival #497 at 4,977 s), 17,546 (arrival #182 at 1,766 s, its fifth request), then 11,504 and 10,111; TraceLab 14,641 (arrival #257), 13,031 (arrival #151), and four between 10K and 12K. Largest completion_tokens in any earlier client.jsonl: 7,318.
findings.fix: Line 711: `aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=timeout, connector=aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=0), read_bufsize=2**22)` (8 MiB lines, valid on every version), then rerun `python3 -m unittest test_program_replay` in the container. To see whether it mattered: `docker exec sglang_hicache python3 -c "import aiohttp, inspect; print(aiohttp.__version__, inspect.signature(aiohttp.ClientSession.__init__).parameters['read_bufsize'].default)"`; 65536 means at risk, 262144 means safe for these traces.

findings.problem: Everything keys on results/.current_run, which names the previous run until this arm's start_server.sh rewrites it (its line 78), and which the launcher never clears. Three effects. (a) watch.sh started within seconds of a relaunch after an outage or hand stop reads the interrupted run and exits at once with 'has not grown for N s'. (b) After a reboot stop_server.sh and start_server.sh test, and may kill, whatever now owns the old server.pid number; server pids restart low in a fresh container. (c) If start_server.sh exits before rewriting the pointer (port still busy, 'a server is already running'), lines 52-56 look in the previous run: a rerun of the same label, or a label that is the tail of the previous one after an underscore (`full` after `ec_full`), is recorded DONE from the old run. c26 was immune to (c): its check read the compare dir this arm's own run_compare.sh had just created (c26.sh:32-33). Today's queues cannot hit the tail case, and prefix labels are safe everywhere: `grep -q "^$L "` is anchored with the trailing space, and `programs_*_L` must end in `_L`.

findings.problem: What the watcher misses or reports wrongly, beyond the stale pointer above. (a) A hung boot: start_server.sh's wait loop ends after 2,400 passes without failing (40 minutes, up to 160 if /health hangs for its 3 s each pass); only then does the client's health check fail and the launcher STOP. Until then there is no traceback and no client file, so the watcher is silent. The same holds for a client stuck before it creates client.jsonl, which exists only after the trace is loaded (about 1 minute for FreeInference 16w, about 75 s for TraceLab): line 22 `[ -f "$c" ] || continue`. (b) `ALL DONE` goes to stdout only, so a clean end reads as 'launcher not running'. (c) Run from any directory but agent_cache/ it sees no log and no pointer and loops silently for ever. (d) Once one traceback or one client error exists in the current run, every restart of the watcher exits at once until that arm ends (as c26's did), so the rest of the arm is unwatched.

findings.problem: Arms 4 and 5 only: a turn whose table has no entry to pick is treated by the engine exactly like a session's last turn. It is registered as ended (first in line for eviction) and no read is planned. The client keeps one table per agent system (harness, model) and an entry needs 5 finished gaps, so the first turns of every system go out with only the `_end` entry. This is a handicap that arms 1 to 3 do not carry, and it is about 8 times more frequent than in campaign 26.
findings.evidence: Engine: `if entry is None or entry.ended or entry.p50 is None: return None`, then `# The session ended (or the client sends no hints): evict it first.` with `next_use=None`. Real log, probe 20261119_022542 (FreeInference x1, this engine): 162 of 632 picks were `entry=none`; all 162 were followed by `nue_register ... next_use_ms=ended` and none got an `ntp_plan` (449 of 449 entry picks did). Simulated 2 h arm, real client code on the real traces with seed 0 (729 arrivals; service time modelled, so shares are estimates): FreeInference 421 of 18,752 non-final hints (2.2 %; about 6 % of hints in the first 30 minutes, about 1 % after; 83 systems appear), TraceLab 118 of 6,546 (1.8 %; about 5 % then 0.4 %). Campaign 26 ec_full: 29 of 12,161 picks (0.25 %).
findings.fix: No change needed to launch. In the write-up, count per arm the non-final requests with `hint.matched == null` in client.jsonl and give TTFT for arms 4 and 5 with those turns excluded, or from minute 30 on. To remove it instead (a change of table scope, the author's call): in `hints_for`, also feed every gap to one run-wide OnlineGapTable and add its `*` entry whenever the system's own list has none.

findings.problem: The exact gap of arms 2 and 3 is not the wait the client sleeps when the next request also waits for a subagent (a join). The hint carries the next request's `wait`, which the converter measures from the latest dependency's end (the subagent's last request), while the stream is really idle from its own reply until the subagent finishes plus that wait. The engine then expects the turn within about a second, the plan expires 60 s later and ends the session. In arms 4 and 5 the same short wait is filed under the spawning reply's key (`task`). FreeInference only; TraceLab has one stream per session.
findings.evidence: `gap = self.scaled_wait(reqs[k + 1])` versus `ready = max((self.end_at.get(tuple(d), ...) for d in r["deps"]), ...)`; `sleep_until(min(ready + rep.scaled_wait(r), rep.deadline))`. Simulated FreeInference arm: 8 of 18,648 exact hints differ from the sleep, by up to 311 s (rid c12-t0: hinted 0.771 s, slept 311.5 s, next deps [[0,0],[1,20]], reply key task). In the trace: 51 such requests among the 107,107 requests of the 3,787 sessions under the cap. All other 18,640 hints, and all 6,503 in TraceLab, equal the sleep exactly.
findings.fix: Small enough (0.04 % of hints) to launch as is and state in the campaign's DECISIONS.md. If fixed: at :387 use the recorded span when the next request has other dependencies, `nxt = reqs[k + 1]; gap = self.scaled_wait(nxt) if nxt["deps"] == [[s, k]] else min(self.args.gap_cap, max(0.0, nxt["t"] - end_of(reqs[k])) * self.args.gap_scale)`, and at :398 observe only when `reqs[k]["deps"] == [[s, k - 1]]`.

findings.problem: Requests still in flight 30 s after the deadline are cancelled without any record, and the `cancelled` record counts plays, not requests. In a saturated run about 80-120 users are waiting on the server at 7,200 s, so the slowest requests of the last minutes vanish, more of them in slower arms. Plays cancelled there also write no play record, and users still at the door leave no record at all, so the door wait and the number admitted cannot be read from play records.
findings.evidence: `send` writes `rec` only after `await self._post_with_retry(...)`, which catches `Exception`; CancelledError is not one. `_wait_all`: `for t in pending: t.cancel()` then `self.write({"kind": "cancelled", "tasks": len(pending), ...})`. Probe tl_ours_x10_a01: 30 in flight at 1,500 s, profile 602 -> 621 at the summary, `{'kind': 'cancelled', 'tasks': 11, 't': 1530.002}`, 87 play records for 98 plays started; so 11 requests left no record.

Analysis rule: pair requests by (inst, k), compare arms only on requests with t_send < 6,900 s that exist in all five arms, and report per arm the users admitted (distinct `play` in req records) out of the 729 arrivals. Optional code change: in `send`, catch asyncio.CancelledError around the post, write the record with `"cut": true`, re-raise, and drop such records in program_summary.py.

findings.problem: The staleness check cannot see a server that stops serving without erroring (for example every queued turn waiting on an SSD read under wait_complete). The client's monitor appends a `lanes` record and flushes every 60 s whatever the server does, so client.jsonl never ages past 300 s while the client process lives.
